run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T02:23:53Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: frontend-proxy is genuinely returning 5xx: over 2026-11-15T01:23:53Z–02:45:18Z it produced 143.203125 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on 'ingress' and 94.453125 on 'router frontend egress'. Sampled error spans are HTTP 504 after ~15.0 s (an Envoy-style route timeout) or HTTP 503 after 0.2–0.9 s where the child 'router frontend egress' span carried http.status_code "0" (no upstream response). The underlying failures sit one hop upstream at frontend: its own error spans are client calls to grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem (52.85), CartService/GetCart (23.38) and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (18.30) plus 7.11 tcp.connect failures, and its server spans for /api/cart and /api/checkout fail together with them. Within 02:20–02:45 every frontend error span fell in the single minute 02:27:00–02:28:00, immediately after the cart Deployment rollout that replaced pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 with cart-84889c965d-tkxdz (created 02:26:23, old pod killed/deleted 02:26:26); in that same minute the new cart pod was CPU-throttled ~90% of CFS periods against a 45m CPU limit (old pod 17–43%). cart and checkout show no error spans of their own, so the failures look transport-level rather than cart application errors. Separately, ~24 proxy spans exceeded 15 s: verified trace 2150204d1e08a291ca29cde87eaf402b shows a 15.0 s proxy 504 while frontend /api/data ran 26.66 s because ad's GetAds took 22.20 s and ad→flagd ResolveBoolean calls ended with gRPC status 4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED). I could not verify the alert's own metric: no RequestErrorRate rule (indeed no alerting rules) is loaded in this Prometheus, proxy error spans are zero from 02:17 to 02:26, and the dominant burst postdates the stated alert start 02:23:53, so why the alert fired at that instant remains unresolved.

claims.text: frontend-proxy produced 143.203125 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on operation 'ingress' and 94.453125 on 'router frontend egress' (increase over the 4885 s window ending 02:45:18Z); its non-error spans in the same window were 22299.876923 on 'ingress' and 22352.890625 on 'router frontend egress'.

frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans are confined to the two operations 'ingress' (143.203125) and 'router frontend egress' (94.453125) when grouped by span_name and http_status_code over the window.

Sampled frontend-proxy error spans are HTTP 504 after ~15.0 s (e.g. ingress span 7cc133ddceb044cb, 15.002046 s, error=true, http.status_code 504, otel.status_code ERROR) and HTTP 503 after 0.2–0.9 s (e.g. ingress span d430a85b26693aee, 0.893138 s, http_status_code 503), each with a child 'router frontend egress' span carrying error="true" and http.status_code "0".

Trace 2150204d1e08a291ca29cde87eaf402b shows the timeout path: load-generator GET error 504 at 15.024 s, frontend-proxy 'ingress' 504 at 15.002 s with 'router frontend egress' http.status_code 0 at 15.002 s, while the frontend server span 'GET' ran 15.2 s (http 200), 'GET /api/data' ran 26.661 s, frontend client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds ran 26.661 s, the ad server span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds ran 22.199 s, and ad's two flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean client spans ended error=true with rpc.grpc.status_code "4" after 1.402 s and 6.302 s.

Trace a6f650436df77a01587a5f9d244bd599 (02:05:51Z) shows the fast-failure path: a frontend-proxy 'ingress' span with error=true and http.status_code 503 after 0.828 s whose 'router frontend egress' child had http.status_code 0, and the trace contains no frontend span at all.

frontend's own error spans over the window are on cart/checkout dependencies: GET /api/cart 23.371, POST /api/cart 52.839, POST /api/checkout 18.290, executing api route (pages) /api/cart 76.230, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 18.295, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 52.852, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 23.377, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 18.295, tcp.connect 7.115, GET /api/data 0.

In 02:20–02:45 all frontend error spans occurred in the single minute 02:27:00–02:28:00 (GET 46, GET /api/cart 46, POST 140, POST /api/cart 104, POST /api/checkout 36, executing /api/cart 150, executing /api/checkout 36, CartService/AddItem 104, CartService/GetCart 46, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 36, tcp.connect 14); every other minute step in that range shows 0.

Per-service STATUS_CODE_ERROR span counts over the window: frontend 385.16, frontend-proxy 237.66, ad 2.04, fraud-detection 2.04, recommendation 4.07, and 0 for cart, checkout, accounting and payment.

The cart Deployment performed a rollout at 02:26:23–02:26:26: 'Scaled up replica set cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1' and SuccessfulCreate of pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz (Scheduled 02:26:23, cart container Started 02:26:25), then 'Stopping container cart' on pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 (Killing/SuccessfulDelete 02:26:26) and 'Scaled down replica set cart-755465879b from 1 to 0'.

The old (cart-755465879b) and new (cart-84889c965d) cart ReplicaSets carry the same container spec: image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, same env (VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, FLAGD_HOST=flagd) and same resources limits cpu 45m / memory 165Mi, requests cpu 15m / memory 55Mi.

CPU throttling of the cart pods: new pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz had throttled-period ratios 0.904 at 02:28:00Z and 0.891 at 02:30:00Z, then 0.199–0.321; old pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 stayed between 0.175 and 0.427 across 02:06–02:28; frontend stayed at 0.309–0.432 and frontend-proxy at 0.039–0.126 over the same period.

cart and checkout show no application-level failure signals: both have 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, and 100% of cart's and checkout's span-duration histograms fall in the ≤5000 ms bucket over the window (cart 1.0, checkout 1.0); cart's pod has 0 restarts and is Ready.

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with 0 restarts except fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh, which has 1 restart; its previous container terminated OOMKilled at 02:31:53Z with exit code 137 and the container restarted at 02:31:54Z.

frontend-proxy had 24.375 'ingress' spans and 23.359 'router frontend egress' spans with duration above 15000 ms over the window, i.e. only a minority of the 143.2 ingress error spans are 15 s route timeouts.
The kept frontend-proxy error-span sample from Jaeger covers only 02:04:12.603522Z–02:11:44.006872Z, so no span-level status or error detail exists in this evidence for the 02:27–02:28 error burst.

Leading hypothesis: the cart pod replacement at 02:26:23–02:26:26 (old pod deleted while the new cart container started only 02:26:25 and wrote its first log line at 02:26:48) left cart briefly unavailable or unresponsive, and the new cart pod was simultaneously CPU-throttled ~90% of CFS periods under a 45m CPU limit, so frontend's CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder calls failed (including 14 tcp.connect failures); frontend then returned 5xx on /api/cart and /api/checkout, which frontend-proxy recorded as ingress errors and the RequestErrorRate alert saw. Supported by exact timing plus transport-level failures, but not sufficient alone to explain the alert's 02:23:53 start.

Second hypothesis: part of the proxy error rate is 15 s route timeouts on slow frontend responses caused by ad-side flagd latency — the verified trace shows a 15.0 s proxy 504 while frontend /api/data took 26.66 s because ad GetAds took 22.20 s and ad's flagd ResolveBoolean calls ended with gRPC status 4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED). This explains the ~24 spans over 15 s but not the fast 503/no-upstream failures that dominate the error count.

Third hypothesis: chronic CPU throttling of the frontend (0.309–0.432 of CFS periods across 02:06–02:38, unchanged across the window) contributes to slow or dropped responses and thus to proxy 5xx/timeouts, but because it shows no change at the time of the error burst it cannot by itself explain the alert.

cart itself shows no application failure: 0 error spans, all cart spans within the ≤5000 ms duration bucket, and its pod Running/Ready with 0 restarts — so the frontend failures look transport-level (connection/unavailability) rather than cart returning errors.

The span-duration histogram reports no ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span above 2000 ms and no frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span above 2000 ms over the whole window, while the trace fetched by ID contains a 22.199 s ad GetAds span and a 26.661 s frontend client span — the duration histogram is incomplete and cannot be used to size or trend latency.

Rejected: that cart was evicted, OOMKilled or otherwise damaged. Its replacement was a controller-driven Deployment rollout (SuccessfulCreate of cart-84889c965d-tkxdz, SuccessfulDelete of cart-755465879b-rh5r4, Scaled up/down of the two ReplicaSets), the new pod has 0 restarts and no Evicted/OOMKilled termination, and old and new ReplicaSet templates are identical apart from pod identity.

Rejected as the cause of this alert: the fraud-detection OOMKill. The container terminated OOMKilled (exit 137) at 02:31:53Z and restarted at 02:31:54Z, after the only frontend/proxy error burst (02:27–02:28) and after the alert start, and no frontend error spans appear in the 02:29–02:45 steps.

gaps: The alert's own expression and window could not be verified: no rule named RequestErrorRate is loaded in this Prometheus and no alerting rules (type=alert) are returned (both queries returned no_data), so the reported current value 0.01111111111111111 cannot be reproduced from the available series.

frontend-proxy error spans are 0 from 02:17:00 through 02:26:00, i.e. the dominant observed error burst (02:27:00–02:28:00) starts after the stated alert start 02:23:53; what pushed the rate above 0 at that exact instant is unknown (a long alert lookback, or a signal not present in this Prometheus, would be needed).

Jaeger holds no traces after 02:11:44.006872Z, so the 02:26–02:28 cart-rollout burst has no span-level status or error detail; its failure mechanism is inferred from metric counts, Kubernetes events and pod state.

cart pod logs were only partially readable: the filtered read returned a single non-diagnostic line and the unfiltered read was incomplete (newest 40 of 843 matching lines, incomplete=true), so cart's log history for 02:26–02:28 is not fully verified.
The frontend container produced no readable log lines (no_data/0 bytes) for the incident window, so the application-level error text of the failing /api/cart and /api/checkout requests is unknown.
flagd container logs were unreadable/empty (no_data), so the cause of ad's 1.4 s/6.3 s flagd ResolveBoolean gRPC status 4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) calls cannot be confirmed or excluded.

Prometheus queries for rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count / rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket labels and for request/Envoy/kube_deployment metric families returned no_data, so no proxy-internal or deployment-metric view of the incident exists.
The change-history integration is not available in this Run, so what triggered the cart Deployment rollout at 02:26:23 and the flagd rollout at 01:57:08 cannot be established.
next_steps: Retrieve the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule definition for RequestErrorRate (exact PromQL, lookback and threshold) to reconcile the reported 0.01111111111111111 with the observed span counts and the 02:23:53 firing time.

Review the change history for the otel-demo cart Deployment around 02:26:23 (and the 01:55/01:57 redeploys of frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout, valkey-cart and flagd) to identify what triggered the rolling restart.
If cart throttling continues near 0.9, evaluate raising the cart container CPU limit (currently 45m, request 15m), which is the constraint behind the throttling.
Collect frontend and flagd container logs from the node/agent side, since the API returned no lines for them, to capture the exact gRPC error text for the failing cart/checkout calls.
Verify post-incident that frontend-proxy ingress error spans stay at 0 and that cart pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz keeps its throttling ratio low before closing the alert.

query.jq_expr: .items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("^(cart-|flagd-)")) | {name: .metadata.name, created: .metadata.creationTimestamp, containers: [.spec.template.spec.containers[] | {name: .name, image: .image, env: [.env[]? | {name, value}], resources: .resources, args: .args, ports: .ports}]}

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
